newsitem.title: UK: BZW strategists scoop double victory in poll.
newsitem.headline: BZW strategists scoop double victory in poll.

text.p: Investment strategists at BZW on Wednesday scooped a double victory in the annual Extel analysts' poll, coming top in both UK and global strategy categories.

With the votes of fund managers' weighted to reflect the size of funds under their control, Richard Kersley and his UK team came top with a vote of 20.43 percent, beating the HSBC James Capel team led by Robert Buckland into second place with 12.23 percent.
In global strategy, BZW's Michael Hughes and team came top with 20.17 percent, above Andrew Garthwaite at SBC Warburg who won 15.27 percent of the vote.
The vote for the BZW UK team echoed a similar victory in the rival Reuters analysts poll earlier this year.

Kersley said BZW's approach had been to focus on individual sectors rather than just on the UK equity market as a whole -- just as well, since he admitted he had been too cautious on the market's overall performance.
"We've been too conservative on the market but better at picking sectors," he said, citing a bearish view on media stocks and retailers as being one of the key calls of the first half of the year.

Meanwhile the position of second-ranked Capel was a sharp improvement on the eighth positive the house scored last year. "We asked clients what they wanted and did our best to try to deliver," Buckland said.

"We have been bullish on the market," he said, "and bullish on the financials, which has been the biggest call for everyone in the first half...and we have warned everyone not to get sucked into anything at the consumer level."
